Candidate changed to r"^(?P<marker>#{1,6})[ \t]+(?P<text>.*?)(?:(?<=\S)[ \t]+#*|[ \t]*)[ \t]*$". The public test: inputs '# C#', '# C# #', '# Title #', '# ##'. Expected outputs: '# C#' => 'C#', '# C# #' => 'C#', '# Title #' => 'Title', '# ##' => '' (empty). Observed actual for '# ##' is '##', failing.

So candidate's regex still captures '# ##' as text '##'? Let's test mentally. For line '# ##', marker '#' (1), text captured by group (?P<text>.*?) which is minimal; after that we have optional group. The line '# ##' has marker '#', then space, then '##' followed by end. The pattern: ^#\s+(?P<text>.*?)(?:(?<=\S)[ \t]+#*|[ \t]*)[ \t]*$.

Let's analyze: after '##', we need to match the optional group. The optional group is (?:(?<=\S)[ \t]+#*|[ \t]*). Option 1: lookbehind preceding non-space then space(s) then zero or more #. Option 2: [ \t]*. But the pattern includes [ \t]* after optional group again? Wait the pattern has [ \t]*$ after the optional group. So final part: optional group then trailing whitespace then end.

So for '# ##', after '##', there is nothing else. The optional group can match [ \t]* (zero spaces). So the group matches empty string. Then [ \t]* after optional group matches zero spaces. So overall match. text group will be '##'? Wait we need to see if the regex is minimal. The text group is '.*?' minimal. It will capture as little as possible while still allowing rest of pattern to match. For '# ##', after marker '#' and space, the rest of line is '##'. To allow optional group to match [ \t]*, we can have zero spaces. But then the '##' must be part of text group. So text group will capture '##'. That's what happened: actual '##'.

But expected empty string. Why should it be empty? Because '# ##' is a heading with level 1 and text '##'? But the test expects empty string for '# ##'. Because maybe the rule: attached hash suffix after title should be considered part of title, but if the title is only hash characters, maybe they should be stripped? The spec: "Attached hashes remain literal title text, including when followed by trailing whitespace or by a separate closing run." So '# ##' should produce '##'? Wait the public test expects empty. Let's understand: '# ##' is a heading with marker '#', title text '##'? Actually the title is '##', but maybe because the title consists only of hash characters, and the regex should strip them? But the rule says attached hashes remain literal title text, including when followed by trailing whitespace or by a separate closing run. So '# ##' should produce '##', not empty. But test expects empty. That means the test expects that a heading where the title is only hashes should be considered empty heading. So the candidate's logic fails: it returns '##' instead of ''.

Thus candidate is not meeting contract. The baseline might have same issue? Baseline regex: r"^(?P<marker>#{1,6})[ \t]+(?P<text>.*?)[ \t]*#*[ \t]*$". For '# ##', text group minimal: '##'? Because trailing #* will match '##', but there is no trailing whitespace. So pattern: after text group, [ \t]* matches zero, #* matches '##', [ \t]* matches zero. So text group gets ''? Wait the #* consumes '##', so text group minimal is empty. Yes baseline would produce '' for '# ##'. So baseline passes this test. Candidate fails.

Thus we must decide: does the task require to keep baseline behavior? The objective: "Repair attached literal hash suffix corruption in MarkdownFile heading titles only. Current source "# C#" becomes title "C" and both heading/section lookup by "C#" fail. Within already recognized ATX lines, only a terminal run of hashes separated from preceding title by a space or tab is a closing marker. Attached hashes remain literal title text, including when followed by trailing whitespace or by a separate closing run. Preserve current trimming and separated closer behavior, empty titles, levels, source line numbers, fence exclusion, hierarchy boundaries, lookup semantics and exact original content."

Thus baseline had correct behavior for '# C#': it produced 'C#'? Let's test: baseline pattern for '# C#': after marker '#', space, title 'C', then space? The regex: [ \t]*#*[ \t]*$ at end. It will match 'C#'? Wait: text group minimal: 'C', then [ \t]* matches space? Actually after 'C', there is '#', so [ \t]* matches zero, #* matches '#', [ \t]* matches zero. So text 'C'. So baseline produces 'C', which is wrong because we want 'C#'. So baseline fails for '# C#'. Candidate fixed that by adding a negative lookbehind: (?<=\S)[ \t]+#* or [ \t]*. That ensures that if there is a space before the # run, it's considered closing. But if attached hash directly after title without preceding space, it's part of title. So for '# C#', after 'C', there is '#', no space. The optional group: either lookbehind pattern requires preceding non-space then space(s) then #*, or [ \t]*. But [ \t]* can match zero spaces. So the optional group can match zero, leaving 'C#' in text group? Wait for '# C#', the string is '# C#'. After marker '#' and space, we have 'C#'. The optional group: we need to match either lookbehind pattern or [ \t]*. Since there is no space before '#', the lookbehind fails. [ \t]* matches zero. So the optional group matches empty. Then [ \t]* after optional group matches zero. So text group captures 'C#'. Good.

For '# ##', after marker '#' and space, we have '##'. The optional group [ \t]* matches zero. So text group captures '##'. That's wrong. So we need to treat the case where title is only hash characters? The public test expects empty. So we need to modify regex to consider when title consists solely of hash characters and no other non-hash content. The baseline pattern would produce empty. But the new requirement says attached hashes remain literal title text, including when followed by trailing whitespace or by a separate closing run. It doesn't say about when title is only hashes. But public test says empty.

Thus the requirement may be to treat titles that are only hashes as empty. So we need to adjust regex to produce empty for '# ##'.

How to fix? We need to modify regex: after capturing text group, ensure that if text is only hash characters, we treat it as empty. Could do: (?P<text>[^#]*?)? But that would exclude hash characters. But we want to allow other characters, but if text consists only of hash characters, produce empty.
